posts.blurb: Cryptic flyers with a stick figure named Percy went up around San Francisco this month. Text the number and you are in a citywide puzzle hunt, free, running through August 7.

posts.blurb: Chris Dutton entered Key West's Hemingway look-alike contest seven times before winning, and he did it clean-shaven as the young Hemingway, in a sweater handed down by the 2009 champion.
posts.why: A 45-year-old contest with judges, dynasties and a scholarship fund — people competing at something strange, seriously.

posts.headline: A Minnesota town now boasts the world's tallest nutcracker. Its pieces were crafted in Utah

platforms.name: Instagram
platforms.why: a 65-foot nutcracker over open prairie needs no caption — feed post

platforms.name: X
platforms.why: the number in the headline is the whole post

posts.blurb: Luverne, Minnesota has about 5,000 residents and 7,554 nutcrackers, and now a 65-foot one dressed as Uncle Sam standing over the prairie. The record it beat, set in Germany, was 33 feet.
posts.why: A town that built a landmark out of one woman's collection — the roadside-attraction story we most want to point at.

posts.blurb: A Victorian electric railway gets you up Snaefell, the highest point on the Isle of Man, where legend says six kingdoms are visible, counting the Heavens. The cache is under a pile of stones.
posts.why: The purest version of what we build: a real climb, a local legend, and a container you have to find.

posts.headline: All together now: Connellsville group hopes to set world record

platforms.why: one absurd number and a date, link preview does the rest

posts.blurb: All thousand rafts were spoken for by March. On August 1 Connellsville, Pennsylvania will try to link 621 people on the Youghiogheny and take a record Portland has held since 2013.
posts.why: A whole river town organizing around one shared physical task — the same social shape as a route full of teams.
